basics.name: Taha Ali
basics.label: Associate Professor • Researcher • Writer
basics.summary: Academic, researcher, and writer working at the intersection of computer networks, information security, emerging technologies, and technology policy.

work.name: National University of Sciences and Technology
work.summary: Associate Professor in the NUST School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (SEECS).
highlights: Teach undergraduate and graduate courses including computer programming, computer networks, network security, cryptocurrencies, and blockchain.
Head the Cognet Lab, researching security applications in emerging technologies including blockchain, machine learning, computer vision, and Internet of Things.
Supervised 25 Masters students and 2 PhD students to graduation.
Introduced a Masters-level course on Cryptocurrencies and Blockchain Technology at NUST in 2018.

work.name: Newcastle University
highlights: Worked on an EU project on secure and verifiable electronic voting systems.
Contributed to research projects on cryptocurrencies and blockchain.
Contributed to the book Real-World Electronic Voting: Design, Analysis and Deployment.

work.name: University of New South Wales
highlights: Worked on security and green applications of software-defined networks.
Researched data provenance mechanisms for healthcare and IoT devices.

work.name: CSIRO
highlights: Worked on algorithms for reducing energy consumption in residential WiFi networks.
Developed algorithms to adjust the mode and transmit power of WiFi access points in response to user traffic, achieving power savings of up to 40%.

work.name: WorldCALL Broadband Pvt. Ltd.
highlights: Took on engineering and management roles in deploying Pakistan's largest hybrid-fiber-coax broadband network.

courses: Security Mechanisms for Body Sensor Networks
highlights: Thesis: Security Mechanisms for Body Sensor Networks
Supervisors: Vijay Sivaraman and Diethelm Ostry
Courses included Network Management, Advanced Computer Networks, Switching Systems and Design, Satellite Systems and Navigation, and Wireless Communications.
